title: Pasadena
name: Pasadena
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Pasadena's Old Pasadena retail, South Lake Avenue office, and medical office near Huntington Hospital.

sections.html: Pasadena combines a historic retail and entertainment district with a corporate and medical office base that draws on Caltech, nearby research institutions, and Huntington Hospital. An exchange buyer here is usually choosing between Old Pasadena's retail storefronts and the office and medical corridors that surround them, and the underwriting approach differs meaningfully between the two.

sections.heading: Old Pasadena's Historic Retail Draw
sections.html:
Old Pasadena's brick storefronts, many dating to the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, house a dining, entertainment, and boutique retail mix that draws both local residents and regional visitors, giving the corridor a steadier foot-traffic base than a purely tourist-dependent district. Historic preservation review applies to exterior changes on many of these buildings, and a buyer should budget extra time for any facade or signage work as a result.

Parking in Old Pasadena runs mostly through city-operated structures rather than dedicated on-site spaces, and a retail tenant's lease terms often assume that shared parking arrangement continues without interruption. A buyer should confirm there is no pending change to nearby structure operations or pricing before assuming current foot-traffic patterns will hold through a full hold period.

sections.heading: South Lake Avenue's Office and Retail Mix
sections.html:
South Lake Avenue functions as Pasadena's secondary commercial spine, combining mid-rise office buildings with street-level retail in a format that leans more corporate and less tourist-driven than Old Pasadena a few blocks away. Office tenants here skew toward financial services, insurance, and professional firms serving the surrounding San Gabriel Valley population rather than the entertainment-industry tenants common closer to Hollywood or Burbank.

Street-level retail along this corridor leans toward regional and local retailers rather than the national chains found in larger malls nearby, and vacancy tends to move with the office towers above rather than independently, since daytime office population is a meaningful driver of lunch and after-work foot traffic for these smaller storefronts. A buyer should review office occupancy in the same building or block before underwriting a ground-floor retail lease renewal, and should expect rents here to run below comparable Downtown Los Angeles office product given Pasadena's position outside the core Los Angeles office submarkets.

sections.heading: Medical Office Tied to Huntington Hospital
sections.html:
Huntington Hospital anchors a cluster of medical office buildings in Pasadena that behaves similarly to the Westwood medical corridor near UCLA, with demand driven by physician group proximity to the hospital rather than general office market conditions. A replacement buyer should confirm what share of tenant improvement costs on a specific medical suite have already been amortized, since specialized medical build-out carries a higher replacement cost than standard office finish.

Lease renewal probability for a physician practice in this cluster tends to run higher than for a general office tenant, since relocating exam rooms, imaging equipment, and a patient base carries real cost and disruption. That stability is part of what makes a Huntington-area medical building attractive to a 1031 buyer, but it should not be assumed automatically; a buyer should still confirm the specific practice's lease term and any early-termination language before relying on that pattern.

sections.heading: The Pasadena Identification Set
sections.html:
A typical Pasadena list draws from:

  • Old Pasadena retail and restaurant storefronts
  • South Lake Avenue mid-rise office and street-level retail
  • medical office buildings near Huntington Hospital
  • research and light-industrial flex space serving nearby institutions

sections.heading: Caltech and JPL's Indirect Pull on Flex Space
sections.html:
While Caltech and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory themselves are not commercial real estate a buyer can acquire, their presence supports a smaller market for research-oriented flex and light-industrial space leased by contractors, vendors, and spinoff companies working alongside those institutions. A buyer considering this niche should underwrite it as a smaller, more specialized market than Pasadena's broader office and retail base, with fewer comparable transactions to draw on.

Lease terms in this niche often track the funding cycles of the research contracts behind them rather than a standard multi-year commercial term, so a buyer should ask whether a specific tenant's occupancy is tied to a renewable institutional contract or a more open-ended commercial lease before relying on it as a stable, long-term income source.

faqs.q: Does historic preservation review affect Old Pasadena property purchases?
faqs.a: It mainly affects renovation and exterior-change timelines rather than the purchase itself, so a buyer planning facade or signage work should budget extra time for design review before assuming a post-closing schedule.

faqs.q: How is South Lake Avenue different from Old Pasadena?
faqs.a: South Lake Avenue leans more corporate, with mid-rise office buildings and street-level retail serving financial services and professional tenants, while Old Pasadena is a historic dining and boutique retail district drawing both residents and visitors, and ground-floor retail vacancy along South Lake tends to track office occupancy above it.

faqs.q: What drives medical office demand near Huntington Hospital?
faqs.a: Physician group proximity to the hospital drives demand more than general office market conditions, similar to how the Westwood medical corridor functions near UCLA, and that proximity-driven demand tends to hold up even when general Pasadena office conditions soften.

faqs.q: Can an investor directly acquire property connected to Caltech or JPL?
faqs.a: No, but their presence supports a smaller market for research-oriented flex and light-industrial space leased by contractors and vendors working alongside those institutions, which is a realistic niche for a replacement property and one with fewer Los Angeles County comparables to draw on than a standard office or retail search.

faqs.q: What should a buyer check before replacing into a Pasadena medical office suite?
faqs.a: Confirm how much of the tenant improvement cost on that suite has already been amortized, since specialized medical build-out carries a higher replacement cost than standard office finish, and ask whether the practice's lease includes any early-termination or relocation language.
